text:
alex: FYI p99 on /v1/generate jumped to ~1.8s around 07:12. Baseline ~450ms. Affected ~120 requests from ~7 distinct API keys.
cassie: ugh. Any commonalities in payloads? long context or tool calls?
alex: Quick grep shows lots of long user preambles (6-8k tokens) + nested tool call mentions. Model: mpt-70q-8k, infra: A100 pool, microbatch size currently 16.
rui: microbatch 16 is large for those long prompts — could be causing queuing and KV cache pressure. Do we have profiler traces?
alex: Uploaded a short perf snippet to the incident board. Key bits:
```
profiler p99 stack (sample):
  - tok-gen (50%)
  - kv-lookup (20%)
  - kv-evict (8%)
  - tool-call-handler (12%)
  - sched-wait (10%)
```
cassie: kv-evict shows up — sounds like the KV cache is getting churned by different sessions with huge prefixes. If the microbatch groups them, we might be thrashing the per-GPU KV store.
dylan: Also saw long tail around reentrant tool calls where generation pauses for external requests, then resumes. Those sessions keep KV pinned and inflate memory working set.
infra-bot: Notice: autoscaler bumped pool from 6 -> 9 GPUs at 07:15 (policy: cpu/mem thresholds). No infra errors.
alex: Tried repro on staging with a mix of 20 long prompts + tool stubs. With microbatch=16 p99 ~1.2s; microbatch=4 p99 ~520ms but throughput down ~1.6x.
rui: This is classic SLO vs throughput tradeoff. For long-context-heavy workloads we need smaller microbatches or smarter batching heuristics (context-length aware grouping).
cassie: Proposal: implement a quick heuristic in router: if estimated prompt tokens > 4k, force microbatch cap 4 and prefer affinity to warmed GPU with matching KV fingerprint.
dylan: Also we should consider KV hotset isolation: sessions that have active tool loops should get sticky KV allocation (session affinity) to avoid evictions.
alex: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: rollout microbatch=8 default for prod pool serving interactive endpoints and enable session-affinity flag for keys that trigger tool calls.
rui: Can we add an on-the-fly optimizer that samples a small window and picks batch size per-second to hit p95 SLO? E.g., if p95 > target, reduce batch; if p95 stable and queue < X, increase.
cassie: We have adaptive-batcher prototype in /eng-runtime/benchmarks. I'll spin it up against the repro harness.
infra-bot: Deploy note: canary config change (microbatch cap) scheduled at 09:00 in us-west-2, will route 5% traffic.
alex: TL;DR: root cause = combination of very long prompts + reentrant tool loops + large microbatch size -> KV churn + queuing -> p99 spikes. Plan: canary microbatch cap + session affinity + follow-up: implement context-aware batching and KV hotset isolation.
rui: I'll open a follow-up RFC with perf numbers + heuristics. tagging @dylan for KV isolation design.
dylan: I'll prototype session-affinity sticky KV allocation this afternoon.
cassie: I'll run adaptive-batcher against the harness and post results here.
alex: thanks everyone. please add any obs/traces to the incident board link: https://redwood-internal/boards/INC-2090
cassie: :thumbsup:
